children: India’s fiscal deficit stood at INR 4.6 trillion in April-July 2026-27, down from INR 4.7 trillion a year earlier, reaching 26.8% of the full-year target versus 29.9% previously.
Total expenditure rose 12.7% year-on-year to INR 17.6 trillion, while capital spending increased to INR 4.5 trillion from INR 3.5 trillion, reaching 36.9% of the annual target.
Total receipts rose 19.3% to INR 13.1 trillion, supported by higher net tax revenues of INR 8.5 trillion, up from INR 6.6 trillion.
India targets a fiscal deficit of INR 17.0 trillion, or 4.3% of GDP, for 2026-27.

title: India’s Fiscal Deficit Narrows in April-July
